subject: Re: Urgent: CrimsonWare checkout latency spikes — exec lifecycle sync

From: Liam O'Connor <liam@crimsonware.com>

Cc: CrimsonWare Ops <ops@crimsonware.com>
Date: 2028-08-01T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Urgent: Intermittent 5–9s latency spikes impacting checkout (us-east)

Kimberly / Redwood team,

We're seeing repeated latency spikes across several checkout routes in US-East starting ~08:50 UTC (attached CSV). 95th/99th pct token latency jumped from ~380ms to 5–9s, and our throughput dropped ~28% for a 30m window. Error rate (5xx) also ticked up to 0.7% during the same time — customers are experiencing timeouts on payment confirmation.

Sample request ids: crw-req-3371, crw-req-3382, crw-req-3410. We've attached a small telemetry dump (crimson_latency_log_0801.csv) and a screenshot of our checkout errors (crimson_sla_snapshot_0801.png).

This is high-severity for production checkout. Can we get an immediate exec-level bridge and a short plan for an interim mitigation (routing, fallbacks, credits) while you investigate root cause?

Thanks,
Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Platform Reliability, CrimsonWare
liam@crimsonware.com
+1 (415) 555-0199
From: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
To: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, naomi_feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-08-01T09:25:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Urgent: Intermittent 5–9s latency spikes impacting checkout (us-east)

Team — fwd'ing CrimsonWare's report. This needs an exec lifecycle sync and a tight customer-facing coordination cadence. Please treat as P0.

Immediate asks (first 30 minutes):
- Aditya: triage telemetry and provide a hypothesis + quick mitigation (pin/version split, traffic steering).
- Neha / Marissa: draft an external customer update and confirm whether we can provide a temporary routing policy or traffic split to Dedicated capacity.
- Naomi / Rishi: pull SLA history, any recent runtime rollouts or autoscale events; prepare credits/contract options if we need to offer a concession.

I propose a 09:45 bridge (30m) — short call to agree immediate mitigations and customer comm. If you can join earlier with a short readout (09:35) that helps.

Attaching the customer's telemetry. I'll own external comm once we have mitigation steps and timing.

- Kimberly Park
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, naomi_feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-08-01T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Urgent: Intermittent 5–9s latency spikes impacting checkout (us-east)

Quick triage notes (09:35):
- Observed pattern: correlated 95/99 spikes on routes using model: open-latest-v2-small for short completions (<= 64 tokens). Spikes line up with autoscaler churn events and a recent runtime kernel selector change rolled 07-31 23:12 UTC.
- Hypothesis: cold KV cache eviction + kernel selection regression under short sequence workloads, causing repeated slow-path kernels for hot prefix. Autoscaler scaling policy shows transient node termination in the warm pool at the exact timestamps.
- Immediate mitigations (low risk):
  1) Pin affected routes to prior runtime kernel profile (rollback selector) — can be done in config within 10m;
  2) Increase warm pool target on Dedicated pool for CrimsonWare to absorb burst (need capacity approval);
  3) Enable route-level KV sticky caching for customer (preserve prefix cache) — toggle in console, immediate;
  4) If capacity available, split 30% of traffic to CrimsonWare's Dedicated capacity or a higher-tier pool to avoid noisy neighbor.

I'll prepare a one-click rollback for kernel selector and test on a canary route. Attaching the relevant runbook excerpt (redwood_runbook_v3.pdf).

- Aditya
Senior Systems Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Urgent: Intermittent 5–9s latency spikes impacting checkout (us-east)

Draft external update (please edit; short + specific):

Subject: Update — Redwood investigating elevated checkout latency (US-East)

Hi Liam —

Thanks for the heads up and the telemetry. We’re actively investigating a pattern of elevated 95th/99th latency on checkout routes in US-East. Immediate actions we’ve taken:
- Enabled sticky KV caching for your checkout routes;
- Initiated a rollback of a recent runtime kernel selector change for a canary route;
- Standing up a dedicated 09:45 bridge with Redwood engineering and ops to confirm next steps.

Next steps we will confirm on the bridge (ETA 09:45 PT):
- Whether we will split a portion of traffic to a dedicated capacity pool;
- A validated rollback plan (timeboxed) and monitoring checks;
- Any short-term credits if the impact crosses agreed SLA thresholds.

We’ll follow up with a short summary after the bridge with timing for mitigation and any customer-facing actions.

Best,
Neha (on behalf of the Redwood team)

Also: Marissa — please draft the customer-facing doc for our portal; Naomi/Rishi please confirm available Dedicated capacity and potential credit sizes (if needed).

Subject: Re: Urgent: Intermittent 5–9s latency spikes impacting checkout (us-east)

Liam — quick update from the bridge (10:05 PT):

What we confirmed:
- Root cause hypothesis: interaction between a kernel selector rollout and warm-pool autoscaler churn leading to repeated slow-path kernel execution for hot prefixes.
- Immediate mitigations we enacted: enabled KV sticky caching for your checkout routes; rolled back the kernel selector for a canary route; and prepared a traffic-split plan to move 30% to Dedicated capacity if you approve.

Next steps (timeline):
- 10:20 PT: Monitor canary for 15 minutes; if stable, roll rollback to 100% (estimated 10–15m).
- 10:30 PT: If issues persist, execute traffic split to Dedicated pool (30% traffic) — will require brief capacity warm-up (3–5m).
- 11:00 PT: Post-mortem readout and customer summary.

We’ve attached the telemetry we discussed and an excerpt from our runbook. If you want us to proceed with the traffic split now, confirm and we’ll action immediately.

Apologies for the disruption — we’ll make the bridge notes and a short customer summary available right after the 11:00 readout.

- Kimberly Park
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Appreciate the quick coordination.
